purpose: Document first-party local registry/map evidence and bounded anonymous geometry access review.
assessment: The Ministry’s Swahili page names Arusha City among e-Ardhi councils. The platform requires an account for requests and application tracking. The public land-rent assessment page accepts title/plot IDs, owner type/name, area, block, and plot number; it is not a geometry-only service. No field was submitted and no account/login used. No anonymous parcel geometry was verified.
registryAssessment: The official Ministry of Lands states that e-Ardhi was operational in Arusha City Council and describes it as providing land planning, surveying, title registration, and valuation services. The city council portal itself identifies Arusha City Council but does not expose a cadastral map or registry. This establishes city-specific service coverage, not public parcel geometry.

officialPrimarySources.observation: Official Ministry of Lands Swahili article states e-Ardhi was implemented in 20 councils, including Jiji la Arusha (Arusha City), and covers land planning, survey, ownership, title registration and valuation.
Official Ministry e-Ardhi page explains that users need an account to request land services and track applications.

Official ministry public land-rent assessment form asks for owner type, region/district, title number, plot ID, personal/institution name, area, block and plot number. No fields were filled or submitted.
Official Arusha City Council portal; no public cadastral or parcel feature service was exposed in the reviewed page.
